jobs.occupation: Customer Solutions Engineer, Composites
jobs.description:
Jupiter Bach is taking the next step in its development as a partner to the global wind industry. Building on our strong position within composite manufacturing, we are expanding our capabilities across engineering, assembly and full-system delivery, supporting leading wind OEMs globally.

This means getting involved earlier in the customer dialogue and taking greater ownership of how customer requirements translate into technically sound and commercially viable solutions.

As our new Customer Solutions Engineer, Composites, you will be an important part of that development.

The opportunity

You will work at the intersection of customers, Sales and Engineering, shaping composite solutions from early customer engagement through to handover to Product Execution.

Your role is to understand the customer need, challenge and clarify requirements, and apply your composite engineering expertise to develop the right solution. Working closely with customer technical teams and specialists within Jupiter Bach, you will drive the technical dialogue and pre-project activities while considering both engineering feasibility and commercial implications.

This is a role for an engineer who wants to use technical depth beyond the traditional engineering function. You will be close to the customer, influence solutions at an early stage and help create a strong foundation for successful engineering and execution.

What you will work with

You will take responsibility for the technical side of customer opportunities during pre-sales and early project phases.

A key part of the role will be to:

• Act as the technical interface towards customers during pre-sales and early project phases

• Translate customer requirements into feasible composite engineering solutions

• Apply your understanding of composite structures, loads, geometry and strength to solution development

• Support Sales in customer meetings, proposals and negotiations

• Drive pre-project activities and technical alignment between customers and internal specialists

• Prepare and validate technical cost calculations and provide input to pricing decisions

• Assess engineering changes and their technical and commercial impact

• Support customer claims through root cause analysis and corrective actions

• Work within PPAP and APQP4Wind processes to ensure quality and robustness

You will be part of a growing team that combines different technical competencies with ownership of specific customers and opportunities.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for an engineer with strong composite expertise who is motivated by applying that knowledge in a customer- and solution-oriented role.

You understand how composite products move from requirements and design through manufacturing and into serial production. Just as importantly, you can communicate your technical knowledge and work effectively with customers, engineers, manufacturing specialists and commercial colleagues.

We expect you to bring:

• An engineering background in Composites, Materials, Structural or Manufacturing Engineering, or another relevant discipline.

• Experience with the design and manufacturing of composite structures or GFRP products

• Understanding of load conditions, geometry and strength evaluation in composite design

• Relevant experience from the wind industry or another technically complex manufacturing environment

• Good understanding of manufacturing processes and engineering interfaces

• The ability to balance technical, operational and commercial considerations

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills

• Professional fluency in English

Experience with PPAP and APQP4Wind is an advantage. Danish language skills are an advantage but not a requirement.

Why Jupiter Bach?

Jupiter Bach is expanding from a strong composite manufacturing base towards broader engineering and full-system capabilities.

For an experienced composites engineer, this creates an opportunity to move closer to the customer and influence solutions much earlier in the process.

You will join an international organisation working with leading wind OEMs and have the opportunity to contribute directly to how Jupiter Bach develops its future engineering and customer solution capabilities.

Contact

For more information about the role, please contact recruitment partner, Lotte Christensen, at loc@slaterconsult.com.

Slater Consult is Jupiter Bachs’s recruiting partner for this position.

jobs.occupation: Join the Crew at Moxy Aarhus
jobs.description:
Are you ready to be part of something from the very beginning? In February 2027, we will open the doors to a brand-new Moxy hotel in Aarhus, and we are now looking for the stars who, together with the management team, will help shape the hotel’s energy, culture and guest experiences from day one.

Moxy is not a traditional hotel. We combine design, energy, technology and personal service in a relaxed atmosphere where guests feel welcome from the moment they arrive. The hotel is operated by Core Hospitality and is part of Marriott International, the world’s largest hotel company.

We are looking for enthusiastic, service-minded colleagues for the following roles:

• Front Office Leader

• Bar Leader

• Breakfast Leader

• Housekeeping Leader

• Front Desk Crew (day and night shifts)

• Bar Crew

• Breakfast Crew

• Housekeeping Crew

What all roles have in common

Regardless of which role you apply for, you will be an important part of the Crew bringing our new hotel to life. We are looking for colleagues who want to make a difference, bring positive energy and help create a workplace where both guests and colleagues feel welcome.

At Moxy, great service is not about stiff formalities. It is about being present, approachable and creating memorable experiences in a personal and relaxed way. We support each other across departments, take responsibility and find solutions when things do not go quite as planned. We believe the best results come from making the most of each other’s strengths and working together as a team.

You do not necessarily need previous hotel experience. What matters most is that you greet people with a smile, are eager to learn and contribute positively to the team. At the same time, we expect you to be ready to roll up your sleeves, remain flexible in a role with varied tasks and be excited about building something new together with the rest of the team.

Who are you?

What matters most to us is not necessarily where you come from, but what you bring to the table.

We imagine that you:

• Have a positive, service-minded approach to guests and colleagues.

• Thrive in an environment where no two days are quite the same.

• Take responsibility for your tasks and actively contribute to the team.

• Are enthusiastic, curious and ready to be part of the journey from day one.

• Enjoy creating great experiences and finding solutions, even when things get busy.

Experience in the hotel, service or restaurant industry is an advantage for several of the roles. For leadership positions, we naturally expect relevant experience and a willingness to take responsibility for both daily operations and the well-being of your colleagues. Across all roles, we place great value on personality, motivation and potential.

What we offer

• The opportunity to help open a brand-new hotel.

• A modern and dynamic working environment full of energy.

• Good working conditions and dedicated colleagues.

• Great opportunities for professional and personal development.

• A strong sense of community, with a focus on teamwork and well-being.

• A workplace where personality, initiative and great ideas are valued.

The recruitment process

The recruitment process is tailored to each role and may therefore vary depending on the position. For some positions, personality assessments or job-related tests may also be part of the process.

How to apply

Depending on the position, your expected start date will be 1 January, 15 January or 1 February 2027, allowing us to prepare together for the hotel’s opening in mid-February 2027.

Submit your application and CV via the link below.

To ensure that all applications are processed correctly and consistently, please apply for the position using the application link in this job posting. Applications submitted directly by email will not be read or considered.

Please clearly state which position you are applying for.

Application deadline: 18 November 2026

We look forward to hearing from you and hopefully welcoming you to our new Crew!

About Core Hospitality

Core Hospitality A/S is one of Denmark’s leading hotel operators, independent of brands and flexible in its approach to operating all types of hotels. Core Hospitality A/S currently operates 18 hotels in Denmark and Norway, including Four Points Flex by Sheraton, Moxy, A Place To Hotel and Kirk Suites.

jobs.occupation: Senior Manager, Clinical Trial Planning
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Overview

**The Senior Manager, Clinical Trial Planning is an individual contributor focused on supporting Clinical Trial Teams (CTTs) in the effective management of clinical trial timelines across the portfolio. The role drives planning system enablement (Planisware), owns and maintains a standardized Microsoft Project (MSP) trial planning template, and develops high-quality timeline visualizations to support trial execution and governance decision-making.

The role partners closely with Global Trial Leaders (GTLs), who are accountable for the overall delivery of their trials and retain ownership of trial timelines within internal planning systems. The Clinical Trial Planner complements this accountability by ensuring planning data is structured, standardized, and translated into clear, actionable insights that enable effective execution and decision-making.

**Responsibilities/tasks

****Planisware Enablement & Trial Support

**

• Partner with GTLs across the portfolio to drive effective use of Planisware and ensure trial plans reflect agreed assumptions, dependencies, and execution strategy, while GTLs retain overall accountability.

• Liaise with Development Program Managers (DPMs) to align trial-level plans with program- and asset-level timelines and milestones.

• Collaborate with the Portfolio Planning team to provide structured trial-level insights and recommendations that inform ongoing refinement and maintenance of Planisware templates and standards.

**MS Project (MSP) Template Ownership & Standardization

**

• Develop and maintain a fit for purpose Microsoft Project (MSP) Trial Planning template for GTL use across study phases.

• Ensure alignment between the MSP template, Planisware, and portfolio-level planning standards.

• Provide guidance to GTLs to promote consistent, high-quality timeline development using the MSP template.

**Data Visualization

**

• Develop and deliver clear visualization templates derived from Planisware and/or MSP data, displaying key milestones and activities.

• Tailor visual outputs to support CTTs, governance, and leadership discussions.

**Process & Tool Adoption

**

• Act as a Planisware subject matter expert at the trial-support level.

• Reinforce GTL training through hands-on guidance and real-time coaching.

• Apply and promote standardized planning methodologies and visualization standards across the portfolio.

**Governance Awareness & Decision Support

**

• Prepare timeline views and supporting materials aligned with governance forum expectations (e.g., Project Board, Portfolio Board, Operational Review Committee).

• Anticipate governance triggers based on timeline changes or emerging risks.

• Translate planning data into concise, decision-ready visuals and summaries.

**Requirements/Preferences

****Senior Manager

**

• Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.

• Approximately 7-10+ years of experience in clinical trial operations, project management, trial planning, or related roles.

• Demonstrated experience driving planning system adoption and influencing cross-functional stakeholders.

• Experience developing or standardizing planning templates, tools, or reporting frameworks across multiple studies.

• Strong understanding of portfolio-level planning considerations and governance expectations.

• Advanced analytical capability and ability to provide structured execution insight to leadership forums.

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$131,040.00---$196,560.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

jobs.occupation: Dynamic flood exposure in Denmark: where will people live when the water comes?
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Environmental Science programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Dynamic flood exposure in Denmark: where will people live when the water comes?

Research area and project description
The overarching aim of this PhD project is to understand how flood exposure in Denmark evolves over time as a result of household location decisions, and to make that dynamic available for cost–benefit analysis of climate adaptation. This is a quantitative PhD: the work combines applied econometrics on Danish register and property-transaction data, a discrete choice experiment, and agent-based simulation modelling. The project is co-financed by the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) and Aarhus University, and the PhD student will be part of the research environments at both institutions.

The project in a nutshell: Cost–benefit analyses of flood adaptation in Denmark evaluate investments over horizons of 80–100 years, yet they treat the spatial distribution of people, buildings and assets as fixed at today's values. Over the coming decades, urban development, demographic change and the gradual repricing of flood risk by insurers, banks and public authorities will reshape who lives in flood-prone areas and what is at risk. At the same time, Danish evidence suggests that flood risk is only weakly reflected in property prices and settlement patterns – households appear to locate under incomplete information about the risk they face. This PhD project treats flood exposure as an emergent outcome of household behavior rather than a fixed physical quantity, and develops an agent-based model of household location decisions under bounded rationality that can project exposure to 2075 under alternative scenarios for institutional risk signals: business as usual, insurance repricing, tighter mortgage lending, and full information.

Qualifications and specific competences
Required qualifications:
• An M.Sc. in economics or spatial data analyses or a closely related quantitative field
• Training in econometrics and experience with R, Python or Stata
• Good written and oral EnglishIt is an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have:
• Experience with panel data, difference-in-differences, hedonic analysis or discrete choice modelling
• Experience with large administrative datasets, e.g. Danmarks Statistik registers
• Experience with or curiosity about agent-based modelling
• Reading proficiency in DanishWe do not expect any candidate to have all of these requirements. The PhD programme includes training in register data, choice experiment design and agent-based modelling, and you will be supervised closely throughout the scholarship. If you have a solid quantitative foundation and are interested in the questions, we encourage you to apply. The role of the PhD student in this project will be particularly focused on the following objectives: 1) a register-based analysis of who lives in flood-prone areas in Denmark and how residential mobility responds to flood events, using Danmarks Statistik microdata linked to building and flood hazard data; 2) a hedonic price analysis of the extent to which flood risk is capitalized in Danish property prices, including event studies around major flood events; 3) a discrete choice experiment estimating how households respond to explicit risk information and to changed signals from insurers, banks and public authorities; and 4) the integration of these results into an agent-based model that simulates exposure trajectories under alternative institutional scenarios and delivers inputs for flood cost–benefit analysis.

The PhD student will enter a research environment with a strong focus on climate adaptation. At the Department of Environmental Science, the student will join the Environmental Social Science and Geography section, which works on environmental valuation, flood damage modelling and the economics of climate adaptation. At DMI, the student will be part of the National Center for Climate Research that produce Danish flood hazard data and climate projections for decision-making at national and municipal levels in Denmark. The student will have office space at both institutions and is expected to take part in the daily research life at both.
You must upload a project description about how you intend to approach the objectives of the project.

Project description (½–4 pages): This document should describe your ideas and research plans for this specific project. If you wish to, you can indicate a URL where further information can be found, but the description should be self-contained.

Qualifications and specific competences: The ideal candidate is highly motivated candidate with an M.Sc. degree with specialization in economics and spatial data analyses, or closely related quantitative fields. Demonstrated oral and written communication skills in English are required. The applicant is expected to present results at international conferences and publish them in international peer-reviewed journals. The applicant should be interested in working in an international and interdisciplinary academic environment. The following qualifications are an advantage, but we do not expect any candidate to have them all:

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Environmental Science, Frederiksborgvej 399, Aarhus University, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Senior Researcher Toke Emil Panduro, e-mail: toke@envs.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Researcher Karsten Arnbjerg Nielsen, e-mail: kan@dmi.dk (co-supervisor)For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk 
How to apply
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 15 November 2026 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 January 2027.

Please make a project description (½-4 pages). The project description should describe your ideas and research plans for this specific project. If you wish to, you can indicate an URL where further information can be found.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

jobs.occupation: Executive Director, People & Organisation
jobs.description:
Would you like to shape the people, culture and organisational foundations of one of the world’s leading humanitarian organisations?  

This is an opportunity to bring your global leadership experience to a mission with profound human impact. As Executive Director for People & Organisation (P&O) at the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), you will inspire employees, empower leaders and turn strategy into meaningful change – ensuring that DRC has the people, capabilities, structures and safeguards required to deliver effective humanitarian responses wherever they are needed most. 
 

You will join DRC at an important time and have a real opportunity to influence its global direction and organisation. The global humanitarian system is going through fundamental change, and you will help shape and adapt organisational structure, operating models and staff capacity to the challenges and opportunities of the future. Your portfolio is global and spans organisation and culture, HR and leadership development, surge capacity, safety, legal affairs and Code of Conduct. As a member of the Executive Management Team, you will help shape strategy, and you will lead approximately 200 colleagues across P&O functions in headquarters and countries. 

About the job 

Reporting directly to the Secretary General, you will set the direction for DRC’s global People & Organisation strategy and ensure that it becomes an enabler for DRC’s ambitions. In close partnership with the Executive Management Team and senior leaders, you will create the conditions for talented people to grow and thrive – while strengthening an inclusive, and high-performing culture. 

This role calls for a leader who enjoys moving between strategic ambition and practical delivery. You will ensure that global policies, systems, data, employment conditions and governance provide relevant and timely support to operations. At the same time, you will carry executive accountability for safeguarding, ethical conduct, legal compliance, safety and DRC’s humanitarian surge capacity – areas fundamental to DRC’s mission. 

You will lead and develop an experienced senior team; Global HR, HR Denmark, HR Operations & Analytics, Surge Capacity, Safety, Code of Conduct, Legal, management support, and change, leadership and culture. Based at DRC’s headquarters in Copenhagen, you will work across a global organisation and build trusted relationships with colleagues and partners from many cultures and contexts. 

The impact you will make: 

• 
Shape DRC’s strategy, culture and global P&O agenda. 

• 
Lead organisational change, leadership development and employee engagement. 

• 
Attract, develop and retain the people DRC needs to deliver its mission. 

• 
Ensure effective global P&O policies, systems, services and people insights. 

• 
Oversee safeguarding, Code of Conduct, safety, legal compliance, duty of care. 

• 
Strengthen humanitarian surge capacity. 

About you 

You are a credible executive who is motivated by purpose and energised by complexity. You bring the strategic perspective to see the whole organisation, the judgement to make thoughtful choices and the drive to translate ambition into clear priorities and measurable results. Colleagues experience you as an inclusive and trusted leader with integrity and empathy providing the clarity to make decisions and create momentum. 
 

What you will bring: 

• 
10+ years of senior experience in global organisations and people leadership. 

• 
A strong record of shaping people strategy and leading transformation across complex, international operations. 

• 
Experience of organisational development, including the renewal and design of operating models. 

• 
Broad understanding of governance, compliance, safeguarding, safety and legal matters.

• 
Strong stakeholder management, analytical and communication skills. 

• 
An inclusive, decisive and high-integrity leadership style. 

• 
A relevant master’s degree and fluent English; additional competency in French, Spanish, Arabic and Danish are an advantage. 

All employees in DRC should master DRC's core competencies: Communicating, Taking the lead, Collaborating, Striving for excellence and Demonstrating integrity.
 

We offer 

Contract length: Permanent 

Work location:  Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken S-train station. DRC has recently moved to a newly renovated multi-tenant house (VOX) with a modern look and shared green canteen.  

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and Lederaftalen between Dansk Arbejdsgiverforening and Lederne (agreement for managers), which can be found here: www.lederne.dk. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.  

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit. 

Application process 

If you are motivated by the opportunity to strengthen a global humanitarian organisation through its people, culture and organisational capabilities, we would welcome your application. Korn Ferry is assisting the Danish Refugee Council with the recruitment of the Executive Director, People & Organisation. Please submit your motivated application and CV through the designated recruitment channel. All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered. 

Closing date for applications: Wednesday 11th November 2026  
 

Further information  

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact: Rabea Rehman, Associate | Executive Search at Korn Ferry, E: DRC_PO@KornFerry.com  

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website drc.ngo. 

Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in RNA Biomarkers and Extracellular Vesicle Biology
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment, Roskilde University, invites applications as post-doctoral fellow in RNA cell biology from April 1st or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Description of the post-doc project
A fully funded postdoc position (18 months) at Roskilde University in the research group of Professor Dalgaard, funded by Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond (Independent Research Fund Denmark) through the project "Enabling RNA Biomarker Origin Detection by Multiplexing Extracellular Tracing". The project will develop a multiplexed extracellular RNA (exRNA)-tracing platform capable of identifying the cell-of-origin of secreted RNAs in plasma and cell media samples and will demonstrate its use by tracing RNA released by pancreatic islet cells and adipose tissue, both highly relevant to type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. The platform will be valuable for validating novel RNA biomarkers and for discovering RNA-based therapeutic targets in metabolic disease.

Responsibilities and tasks
The postdoc’s work will include research within ExRNA biology, RNA biomarker discovery, and multi-omics profiling, with focus on tracing the cellular origin of secreted RNAs relevant to type 2 diabetes and metabolic disease. In addition, some amount of teaching is also required. 

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead the development and validation of a multiplexed exRNA-tracing platform, based on integration of bio-orthogonal proximity labeling and metabolic RNA labeling systems.

• Apply proteomics and small RNA sequencing/omics approaches to characterize the RNA and protein cargo of pancreatic islet- and adipose-derived extracellular vesicles and biofluid samples.

Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent within cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, or a related field. Qualifications within the following scientific areas are required:

The ideal candidate has an outstanding track record of accomplishments and a critical mindset. Moreover, an open mentality with focus on research communication, inter-disciplinary curiosity and teamwork will be required to succeed. Moreover, the following qualifications are relevant:

• Certified training in laboratory animal research is required.
• Advanced experimental experience in RNA biology and/or extracellular vesicle (EV) biology is required
• Hands-on experience with proteomics and/or small RNA sequencing or other omics-based biomarker profiling techniques is required.
• Experience with research in metabolic disease, in particular type 2 diabetes or obesity, and/or experience working with pancreatic islets or other metabolically relevant primary cells/tissues, will be highly valuable.
• Experience with publication of original relevant scientific data in peer-reviewed journals will be an advantage.
The ideal candidate should be enterprising and possess good communication skills, be visible and involved in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department and with project collaborators.

Assessment

• The ability to promote and utilize research results.

The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, chemistry, physics, environmental sciences, and mathematics. Bachelor programs are offered within these areas, as are interdisciplinary Master programs. The Department’s laboratories are equipped with modern infrastructure and shared state-of-the art instrumentation. This includes recently acquired NMR, mass spectrometry (LC- and GC-MS, including high-resolution measurements and proteomics), and microscopy (AFM, confocal and fluorescence) instruments, GMO class 1 and 2 labs, flow cytometry, NTA, coulter counter, NGS, Q-PCR facilities, pipetting robots, calorimetry (ITC and DSC), chromatography (HPLC), and scattering (DLS, SAXS) instruments.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment (DSE), Roskilde University, invites applications for a position as assistant professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management, from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is limited for a period of 4 years.

In announcing the position, DSE looks to strengthen its research in environmental sciences within the following fields: Sustainability transitions and circular economy in institutional and healthcare settings, sociotechnical systems analysis, behavioural and consumption analyses, the economic valuation of environmental and health externalities; and the wellbeing economy as a framework connecting these to the circular transition. The Department is interested in applicants who see large-scale, cross-sectoral shifts of this kind - spanning production and consumption systems - as necessary to address today's pressing environmental challenges across the natural- and social-scientific fields represented in the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The position is closely linked to and partly funded by an Innovation Fund Denmark grant for a newly initiated interdisciplinary research project ROUNDS: Rethinking the cost of care – including the cost of externalities in circular transitions. The project links human health risk assessment, ecological economics, and behavioural research to reduce reliance on single-use plastics and textiles in the healthcare sector.

The Department is interested in applicants whose research and teaching profile includes all the above subject areas in combination with an interest in building interdisciplinary research and collaboration on education. The Assistant Professor’s duties will comprise research at a high international level and a strong commitment and contribution to teaching broadly in the environmental science programs at bachelor’s and master’s level. The Assistant Professor will teach in an interdisciplinary environment and engage in problem-oriented project work with extensive student involvement and responsibility.

DSE is one of four departments at Roskilde University. The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, environmental sciences, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Bachelor and Master programmes are offered within these areas. Research and education within the fields take place in a collaborative and interdisciplinary university environment, also spanning collaboration with the other departments, covering social sciences and humanities, where relevant. The department is organised into four Sections comprising the research and education activities.

The Assistant Professor will be part of the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The Section’s current members primarily have a background within one or more of the fields of aquatic ecology, ecotoxicology, biological production (including aquatic biotechnology), and geochemistry. DSE has a well-established shared infrastructure with state-of-the-art equipment facilities, including field spectroradiometer, Mass-spectrometry (LCMS, GCMS, ICP-MS), CHNS, various microscopy facilities and access to workshops.

Read more about the section at https://ruc.dk/en/research-group/environmental-dynamics

Responsibilities and tasks
The assistant professor’s work will include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication, and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within one or more of the fields of the Assistant Professorship and in general activities at the environmental science programme activities.

In addition to research and research-based teaching, the position also requires sharing knowledge with the rest of society - including participation in public debate. To a limited extent, this may also include performance of other activities.

As assistant professor, you are also expected to complete the educational training program for assistant professors at RUC (up to 220 hours). The training programme will give you pedagogical and didactic tools as well as familiarize you with the Roskilde University educational model called Problem oriented project learning (PPL). Applicants are referred to the university’s Faculty expectations (https://ruc.dk/en/working-roskilde-university ) for specifications on the required level of qualifications within research, teaching, networking, fundraising, impact and outreach etc.

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead and further develop research within the circular economy, sustainability transitions, and environmental management in institutional and healthcare settings, including engagement in the research project ROUNDS
• Develop the field of interdisciplinary research by actively collaborating with other scientific fields within the department or at other departments, connecting environmental science with social science and economics
• Contribute to the development of the research profile of the department
• Maintain a significant record of publications
• Collaborate with colleagues in establishing a vibrant research community
• Participate actively in research networks and external research funding activities
• Teach, supervise, and assess students at BSc and MSc levels. This also implies developing the field in relation to teaching
Qualifications
You must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Science or in the interface between the natural and social sciences applied to environmental and sustainability questions. In addition, a documented qualitative and/or interdisciplinary approach to sustainability transitions is required.

Documented research production at international level within one or more of the following scientific areas are required:

• Circular economy and sustainability transitions in institutional or healthcare settings
• Sociotechnical systems theory and analysis of organisational/infrastructural change
• Valuation of environmental and health externalities, including in relation to public procurement
The ideal candidate has:

• Teaching experience within one or more of the fields of the Associate Professor
• A keen interest and experience in project-based, problem-oriented teaching as well as teaching in an interdisciplinary environment
• Documented experience with interdisciplinary research and interdisciplinary collaborations will also be seen as an advantage.
In addition, it will be seen as an advantage if you can contribute to research and teaching within one or more of these areas:

• Environmental management and monitoring
• Political economy of sustainability transitions
• Health systems and behavioural aspects of circular practice
The ideal candidate must be enterprising, possess good communication skills, and be a visible and involved participant in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department.

At the time of appointment, successful candidates must master English for academic purposes.

Assessment
In the assessment of the candidates, consideration will be given to:

• Relevance of research topic
• Scientific production at an international level
• Research prospective and the ability to promote and utilise research results
• Experience in teaching and education
• Other academic experience, e.g. from organising research conferences or seminars
• Ability to contribute to development of the department’s internal and external cooperation
Questions
Potential applicants from outside Denmark will find information about life in Denmark (taxation, healthcare etc.) at www.lifeindenmark.borger.dk

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Section Kristian Syberg on tel. (+45) 4674 3776 or e-mail: ksyberg@ruc.dk or Head of Department Susanne Sørensen by email: susa@ruc.dk.

Terms of employment
The employment is on full time, 37 hours per week and in the daily work you will refer to Professor Kristian Syberg. Your head of staff will be Head of Department Susanne Sørensen.

The position will be filled according to the Agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. 

According to the Pay Transparency Directive, the salary ranges for the various job categories at Roskilde University are listed here. 

Application procedure 
After the deadline for applications the Head of Department will shortlist applicants for assessment with assistance from the recruitment committee including the chairperson of the assessment committee.

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application 
To apply for the position go to www.ruc.dk/en/job/ 

Only applications in English are accepted. 

Applications must include:

• Documentation of education
• Teaching portfolio (read more about teaching portfolio at Roskilde University here)
• A complete list of publications

If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here).

As a Senior Microsoft 365 Platform/System Engineer, you will join a team of dedicated professionals focused on developing SharePoint and Microsoft 365 within our Modern Workplace services.

You will be part of a cross-country, agile Microsoft 365 team comprising 12 dedicated professionals.

At BEC, we value regular in-office collaboration while offering flexibility to work remotely for up to eight days per month. You will report to Anne-Mette Bluhme.

Your primary tasks and responsibilities will include:

• Developing and managing SharePoint Online Services

• Administering and maintaining the Microsoft 365 suite, including Copilot, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams and OneDrive for Business

• Ensuring the availability, performance, and security of these services

• Implementing and managing security controls for Microsoft 365 environments, ensuring compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements

• Participation in development projects of new services

• Developing and maintaining PowerShell scripts to automate administrative tasks and improve efficiency

• Handling second-line Microsoft 365 incidents and service requests

To succeed in this role, you should have:

• Solid experience in SharePoint development and maintenance

• Solid experience administering Microsoft 365 services

• Strong knowledge of Microsoft 365 applications, including Exchange Online, Teams, OneDrive for Business, and Copilot

• Knowledge of Power Apps, Power Automate, and Microsoft Purview

• Fluency in written and spoken English and Danish

• Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills

• Customer-oriented thinking and high-quality standards

• The ability to collaborate effectively across functions and teams

• Curiosity, openness, and a willingness to share knowledge with others

It would also be an advantage to have:

• Familiarity with cloud security and compliance standards

• Knowledge of networking and identity management in cloud environments

• Experience in the financial sector
